claims.text: THE LORING TRAFFIC NEVER SAYS UFO. Its vocabulary is 'unidentified helicopter', 'intruder' and 'AFB Penetration' throughout. The NORAD logs do say UFO, repeatedly, in their own voice. The distinction belongs in the node, because the strength of the Loring material is that it is a nuclear security record rather than a UFO record.

claims.text: The DDO update as of 300600 EST Oct 75 records the rules of engagement approved by the Department of the Army Director of Operations, DCSOPS: the National Guard helicopter and crew placed in full time training duty; entry into Canadian airspace with Canadian consent; employment limited to tracking and identification; and only US military personnel aboard, plus if necessary representatives of the FBI, FAA and Border Patrol.

claims.sourceText: NMCC DDO update as of 292200 EST Oct 75, citing 42 BW CP LORING AFB 291140Z OCT 75 and SAC CP OPS CONTROL 291954Z OCT 75, http://www.nicap.org/reports/751027loring_1-6.htm , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: The escalation reached the Army Staff and the State Department. The DDO update as of 292200 EST records that the Chief of Staff of the Air Force operations division requested the Army National Guard helicopter be provided until 300800 EST 'to track and identify the intruder; no apprehension to take place; the Canadian Border would not be crossed', that the request was under consideration by the Department of the Army Director of Operations, DCSOPS, that a military aide to the Special Assistant to the Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Defense had been advised, and that 'The State Department Canadian Desk Officer has been kept informed.'

claims.nodeLabel: NMCC Memorandum for Record, 'AFB Penetration', 29 October 1975
claims.sourceText: NMCC Memorandum for Record, 29 October 1975, reproduced at http://www.nicap.org/reports/751027loring_1-6.htm , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: The memorandum's five numbered paragraphs read: '1. At 290200 EST AFOC informed NMCC that an unidentified helicopter, possibly two, had been sighted flying low over Loring AFB Maine, in proximity to a weapons storage area. 2. An Army National Guard helo was called in to assist in locating the unidentified helo(s). 3. NORAD was informed of the incident by SAC, requested and received authority from Canadian officials to proceed into Canadian airspace if necessary to locate the intruder. 4. At 0404 SAC Command Center informed NMCC that the army helo assisting on the scene had not sighted the unidentified helo(s). 5. A similar incident was reported at Loring the evening of 28 October 1975.' Signed C. D. Roberts, Jr., Brigadier General, USMC, Deputy Director for Operations (NMCC).

claims.sourceText: NMCC Memorandum for Record and DDO updates, 29 to 30 October 1975, http://www.nicap.org/reports/751027loring_1-6.htm , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: THE DOCUMENT NEVER SAYS UFO. Its vocabulary throughout is 'unidentified helicopter', 'intruder' and 'AFB Penetration'. What it documents is a failure to identify and a failure to intercept at a nuclear weapons storage area, escalated to the Joint Staff, the Army Staff, a Deputy Secretary of Defense aide and the State Department's Canadian desk. That is the whole of the Tier 1 claim and it is enough.

claims.sourceText: NMCC AFB PENETRATION narrative, 29 October 1975, http://www.nicap.org/reports/751027loring_1-6.htm , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: The accompanying AFB PENETRATION narrative records that 'Sightings of the unidentified helicopter(s) were limited to security guards' and that one helicopter landed briefly in proximity to a weapons storage area after penetrating Loring AFB from Canadian territory.

The contemporaneous-paper half of that split is real and checkable. It includes the National Military Command Center's Memorandum for Record of 29 October 1975 on the Loring penetration; the 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log for 7 to 19 November 1975; the Project Blue Book Minot file of October and November 1968 with seven AF Form 117 witness questionnaires; the Project Blue Book telephone log of 1 August 1965 for F. E. Warren; and the 379th Bombardment Wing historian's file of January 1979. All were opened by this board on 19 September 2026.

claims.sourceText: NMCC Memorandum for Record and DDO updates, 29 to 30 October 1975, http://www.nicap.org/reports/751027loring_1-6.htm , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: THE 1975 SEQUENCE IS A NUCLEAR SECURITY RECORD BEFORE IT IS A UFO RECORD, AND THE DOCUMENTS SAY SO IN THEIR OWN WORDS. The National Military Command Center's subject line is 'AFB Penetration'. The Loring traffic says 'unidentified helicopter' throughout and never says UFO. The reporting runs to the Joint Staff, the service chiefs, the DIA, NSA and CIA representatives, the Army Staff Director of Operations and the State Department's Canadian desk. That is what gives this domain its weight: the correlation is visible in operational paper produced by people who were not thinking about the subject this board is about.

claims.sourceText: NMCC Memorandum for Record, 'AFB Penetration', 29 October 1975, reproduced at http://www.nicap.org/reports/751027loring_1-6.htm , opened 2026-09-19
claims.text: SAC is the reporting node in the primary records. The National Military Command Center's Memorandum for Record of 29 October 1975 states that 'NORAD was informed of the incident by SAC' and that 'At 0404 SAC Command Center informed NMCC that the army helo assisting on the scene had not sighted the unidentified helo(s)', citing SAC CP OPS CONTROL 291954Z OCT 75 among its sources.
